newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul foundation collapse kills one, injures three.
newsitem.headline: Seoul foundation collapse kills one, injures three.

text.p: One woman was killed and three people injured on Wednesday when part of the foundation wall of an apartment complex in northern Seoul collapsed onto a neighbourhood below, a police official said.

The Hanjin Apartment Complex, built on a hillside, was still standing and appeared stable, but more than 400 families resident in the buildings above the damaged foundation were evacuated after the collapse, the official said.

He said Kim Mi-sung, 26, was killed in an outdoor public telephone booth when the mixed concrete-and-dirt foundation, some 50 meters (150 feet) wide and 20 meters (60 feet) high, plowed into the booth. The three injured were nearby.
Five passenger cars and two motorcycles were trapped in the heap of earth, he said. It was not clear whether there were more victims.
"Rescue work is continuing, but we don't know whether there are more victims," he said by telephone. "So far, there were no reports indicating more victims."
A three-storey store was partially destroyed by the collapse of the wall, which Yonhap Television News said was caused by heavy rain over the past three days.
The ground floor was buried but the higher floors were not badly damaged, the police official said.
Yonhap said many people were feared trapped in the store because many shoppers were inside when the accident happened.
The official could not confirm the report.
